paragraph_functions: context: Wordle as phenomenal game with hidden information
overview: three models built for tasks
Model-I: LSTM for time-series prediction with interval
Model-II: XGBoost for distribution with R2=0.68
Model-III: SVM-RBF for classification with accuracy 0.6556
additional: interesting observations including human vs ML
closing: letter to NYT editor + keywords
chapter_layouts.counting_method: 7 blocks: context + overview + 3 models + additional + keywords

paragraph_functions: background: Wordle taken world by storm
motivation: help NYT understand difficulty and audience
lit-review-tree: Poirrier/Selby decision tree for Wordle
transition: figure reference to modeling process
ambiguities: Literature review and Our Work within introduction.

paragraph_functions: intro: assumptions made to simplify, properly justified
assumption-1: ignore extreme events like holidays
assumption-3: players report independently without cheating
data-cleaning: two kinds of errors (lexical + data)
LSTM-intro: combines long-term and short-term memory
implementation: Pytorch, single LSTM layer, 5 units, lookback=33

closing: F-test null result for hard mode correlation

paragraph_functions: aspect-decomposition: time vs difficulty for distribution
time-null: wt regression p=0.457, no time correlation
RFE-result: Daily frequency, CharNum, Letter frequency selected
EERIE-result: predicted as hard, consistent with Ew=709.9076
confusion-matrix: easy and medium good, hard weak
ROC-curve: average curve close to upper left
sum-check: 25 test predictions sum within (98,102), variance 0.71
weaknesses: holidays ignored, Twitter bias, rounding errors, SVM weak on hard
salutation: Dear Puzzle Editor with interest expression
LSTM-results: player decline but hard mode percentage rising
XGBoost-results: EERIE distribution prediction with pie chart
SVM-results: difficulty levels and EERIE as hard
closing: model helps increase awareness, good luck

units.source_excerpt: Wordle is a phenomenal network game. Its appearance intensely aroused people's attention. Although it looks tiny, the hidden information behind it is huge and meaningful.
units.reusable_pattern: [Subject] is a phenomenal [category]. Its appearance aroused attention. Although [surface], [hidden value] is [qualifier]
reusable_elements: [Subject] is a phenomenal [category]. Although it looks [surface], the hidden [content] is [qualifier]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'phenomenal' as unsupported superlative

units.source_excerpt: We built three models to finish the tasks. Model I uses LSTM to forecast the number of reported scores in the future. Model II uses seven XGBoost regressors to predict the percentage distribution. Model III classifies words by their difficulties using SVM with RBF kernel.
units.reusable_pattern: We built [N] models. Model I uses [A] to [goal-1]. Model II uses [B] to [goal-2]. Model III [C] to [goal-3] numbered model enumeration
reusable_elements: We built [N] models to finish the tasks. Model I uses [A] to [goal]. Model II uses [B] to [goal]. Model III uses [C] to [goal]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid Roman numeral model naming without justification

units.source_excerpt: Model I: LSTM is an improved recurrent neural network that can solve the long-distance dependence problem that other neural networks cannot handle.
units.reusable_pattern: Model [N]: [Model] is an improved [category] that can solve [problem] that others cannot handle model-label definition
reusable_elements: Model [N]: [Model] is an improved [category] that can solve [problem] that [alternatives] cannot handle
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim superiority without comparative evidence

units.source_excerpt: After 150 times of independent model training, the prediction interval is [20745.72, 22914.74].
units.reusable_pattern: After [N] times of independent training, the prediction interval is [range]
reusable_elements: After [N] times of independent model training, the prediction interval is [range]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report intervals without stating confidence level

units.source_excerpt: Additionally, from the linear regression on the proportion of hard mode with word attributes, we can also find no correlation between hard-mode-ratio and target word.
units.reusable_pattern: Additionally, from [analysis] on [DV] with [IV], we can also find no correlation between [A] and [B]
reusable_elements: Additionally, from [analysis] on [DV] with [IV], we can also find no correlation between [A] and [B]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'we can also find' — state directly 'we found'

units.source_excerpt: Model II: To get the percentage distribution of a given day associated with a specific word, we trained seven separate XGBoost models. The R2 of our model is 0.68, which can be accurately predicted with low uncertainty after testing.
units.reusable_pattern: Model [N]: To get [target], we trained [N] separate [models]. The R2 is [value], which can be [quality] predicted
reusable_elements: Model [N]: To get [target], we trained [N] separate [models]. The R2 of our model is [value]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say 'accurately predicted' for R2=0.68

units.source_excerpt: We apply 'EERIE' to the model and gain a prediction percentage distribution, showing that EERIE should be considered as a problematic word.
units.reusable_pattern: We apply [example] to the model and gain [result], showing that [example] should be considered [label]
reusable_elements: We apply [word] to the model and gain [result], showing that [word] should be considered as [category]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'problematic' — use defined difficulty labels

units.source_excerpt: Model III: We quantified the difficulty of words by the unequally weighted average of percentage distribution and divided them into three levels: easy, medium and hard.
units.reusable_pattern: Model [N]: We quantified [concept] by [metric] and divided into [N] levels: [list]
reusable_elements: Model [N]: We quantified [concept] by [metric] and divided them into [N] levels: [level-list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'unequally weighted' without justifying weights

units.source_excerpt: Then we used labeled to fit SVM model with RBF kernel and gain an accuracy score of 0.6556 and an F1 score of 0.6634.
units.reusable_pattern: Then we used [labels] to fit [model] with [kernel] and gain accuracy [value] and F1 [value]
reusable_elements: Then we used [labels] to fit [model] with [kernel] and gain an accuracy score of [X] and an F1 score of [Y]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'gain' for metric reporting — prefer 'achieved'

units.source_excerpt: Except for these three models, we also found some interesting observations from the dataset, one of which discussed the differences between human thinking and machine learning.
units.reusable_pattern: Except for [models], we also found [qualifier] observations, one of which discussed [topic]
reusable_elements: Except for these [N] models, we also found some [qualifier] observations from the dataset, one of which discussed [topic]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'interesting' — specify what makes observation notable

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we write a letter including our models, results, and advice to the New York Times Wordle editor.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, we write a letter including [content] to [recipient]
reusable_elements: Finally, we write a letter including our [models/results/advice] to [recipient]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'write' present tense when paper is past — use 'wrote'

units.source_excerpt: Keywords: Wordle; LSTM; Recursive Regression; XGBoost; Feature Engineering
units.reusable_pattern: Keywords: [semicolon-separated list]
reusable_elements: Keywords: [Model]; [Technique]; [Domain];
prohibited_generalizations: Do not include generic terms like 'Feature Engineering' as keywords

units.source_excerpt: Nowadays, a puzzle game called 'Wordle' has taken the world by storm with its light-hearted approach and confusing but attractive yellow, green, and grey squares.
units.reusable_pattern: Nowadays, [subject] has taken the world by storm with its [qualities] and [visual-elements]
reusable_elements: Nowadays, [subject] has taken the world by storm with its [qualities] and [visual elements]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'taken the world by storm' cliche

units.source_excerpt: Generally speaking, it is a game that requires players to guess the correct words within less than six times.
units.reusable_pattern: Generally speaking, it is a game that requires players to [action] within [constraint]
reusable_elements: Generally speaking, it is a [category] that requires [actors] to [action] within [constraint]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'Generally speaking' as filler — state directly

units.source_excerpt: To help the New York Times better understand the difficulty and audience of 'Wordle', we hope to construct a prediction model using daily performance data posted by players on Twitter in 2022.
units.reusable_pattern: To help [stakeholder] better understand [aspects], we hope to construct [model] using [data]
reusable_elements: To help [stakeholder] better understand [aspects], we hope to construct a [model] using [data source]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'we hope' — state intent directly

units.source_excerpt: In the time series field, models mainly focus on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), a kind of artificial neural network suitable for processing and predicting important events with very long intervals and delays in time series.
units.reusable_pattern: In the [field], models mainly focus on [technique], a kind of [category] suitable for [capability]
reusable_elements: In the [field], models mainly focus on [technique], a kind of [category] suitable for [processing capability]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim field 'mainly focuses' on one technique

units.source_excerpt: More specifically, the average reduction in the error rate obtained by LSTM compared to ARIMA was between 84% and 87% in forecasting time series.
units.reusable_pattern: More specifically, [metric] obtained by [A] compared to [B] was between [X]% and [Y]%
reusable_elements: More specifically, [metric] obtained by [technique-A] compared to [technique-B] was between [X]% and [Y]%
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite single-study comparisons as general truth

units.source_excerpt: Assumptions are made as follows to simplify the problem. Each of them is properly justified.
units.reusable_pattern: Assumptions are made as follows to simplify the problem. Each is properly justified
reusable_elements: Assumptions are made as follows to simplify the problem. Each of them is properly justified.
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'properly justified' — let justification speak for itself

units.source_excerpt: Ignore the influence of extreme events, such as holidays and natural disasters, since these events rarely happen.
units.reusable_pattern: Ignore the influence of [factor], such as [examples], since [justification]
reusable_elements: Ignore the influence of [factor], such as [examples], since [justification]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss holidays as 'rarely happen' — they recur

units.source_excerpt: Other specific assumptions, if necessary, will be mentioned and illustrated while we're establishing models.
units.reusable_pattern: Other specific assumptions, if necessary, will be mentioned while establishing models
reusable_elements: Other specific assumptions, if necessary, will be mentioned and illustrated while [establishing models]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid deferring assumptions without specifying which sections

units.source_excerpt: Table 1 shows notations that should be used in equations.
units.reusable_pattern: Table [N] shows notations used in equations
reusable_elements: Table [N] shows notations that should be used in equations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define symbols only in tables

units.source_excerpt: After statistics and processing of data, it was found that there were two kinds of errors in the sample data: The first one is the lexical error; The second one is the data error.
units.reusable_pattern: After [processing], it was found that there were [N] kinds of errors: [type-1]; [type-2]
reusable_elements: After [processing], it was found that there were [N] kinds of errors in [data]: [type-1]; [type-2]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid passive 'it was found' — state directly

units.source_excerpt: LSTM, unlike other kinds of artificial neural networks, combines long-term and short-term memory to ensure the stability and accuracy of the model along the time series.
units.reusable_pattern: [Model], unlike other [alternatives], combines [A] and [B] to ensure [qualities]
reusable_elements: [Model], unlike other [alternatives], combines [component-A] and [component-B] to ensure [qualities]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim uniqueness without specifying which alternatives

units.source_excerpt: However, the distribution of the number of reported scores is quite unbalanced. In other words, the traditional Min-Max normalization will not take effect in this situation. As a solution, a natural logarithm will be applied in the first step.
units.reusable_pattern: However, [data-issue]. In other words, [traditional-method] will not work. As a solution, [alternative] will be applied
reusable_elements: However, [data issue]. In other words, [traditional method] will not take effect. As a solution, [alternative] will be applied
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'In other words' restating same idea — consolidate

units.source_excerpt: In our task, we implement LSTM neural network by Pytorch. We aim to predict the score-reported number on March 1st based on the sample data with scores reported for 359 days.
units.reusable_pattern: In our task, we implement [model] by [framework]. We aim to predict [target] based on [data]
reusable_elements: In our task, we implement [model] by [framework]. We aim to predict [target] based on [data]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name frameworks unless reproducibility requires it

units.source_excerpt: We only used one LSTM layer and one fully connected layer because of the small sample. Moreover, after cross-validation, we found that the best number of LSTM units was 5.
units.reusable_pattern: We only used [architecture] because of [reason]. Moreover, after [validation], we found [optimal-config]
reusable_elements: We only used [architecture] because of [reason]. Moreover, after [validation], we found that the best [parameter] was [value]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not justify minimal architecture solely by sample size

units.source_excerpt: Because of the randomness of the neural network, after 150 times of training, we get the following prediction for the reported number on March 1st, 2023.
units.reusable_pattern: Because of [randomness], after [N] times of training, we get [result]
reusable_elements: Because of the randomness of [model], after [N] times of training, we get [result]
prohibited_generalizations: Specify whether 150 runs is bootstrap or ensemble

units.source_excerpt: We choose the 95% confidence interval with the |z| value of 1.96. Therefore, the prediction interval is [20745.72, 22914.74] by 95% confidence.
units.reusable_pattern: We choose the [X]% confidence interval with z=[value]. Therefore, the interval is [range]
reusable_elements: We choose the [X]% confidence interval with the |z| value of [z]. Therefore, the prediction interval is [range]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use z-interval for neural network predictions without normality check

units.source_excerpt: The F-statistics is 1.69, less than 2.397 (alpha=0.05). Therefore, words will not affect the percentage of scores reported in Hard Mode at 5% significance level.
units.reusable_pattern: The F-statistic is [value], less than [threshold] (alpha=[level]). Therefore, [null-result]
reusable_elements: The [statistic] is [value], less than [threshold] (alpha=[level]). Therefore, [conclusion]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not accept null based solely on F < threshold without discussing power

units.source_excerpt: Notice that there are two main aspects for estimating the model, time and difficulty of word. We first verify the correlation between time and the percentage distribution.
units.reusable_pattern: Notice that there are [N] main aspects: [A] and [B]. We first verify [relationship]
reusable_elements: Notice that there are [N] main aspects for [purpose], [A] and [B]. We first verify [relationship]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'Notice that' as imperative to reader

units.source_excerpt: Then we did the linear regression of wt on time and discovered that the p-value of 0.457, which is much larger than 0.05. It shows no significant correlation between performance and time.
units.reusable_pattern: Then we did [analysis] of [DV] on [IV] and discovered p-value=[value], much larger than [threshold]. No significant correlation
reusable_elements: Then we did [analysis] of [DV] on [IV] and discovered that the p-value of [value], which is much larger than [threshold]. It shows no significant correlation
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'much larger' for p=0.457 — say 'substantially exceeds'

units.source_excerpt: To reduce the impact of outliers in the model, RobustScaler is used to normalize the data. Therefore, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) algorithm was used to rank those six features.
units.reusable_pattern: To reduce [issue], [Scaler] is used. Therefore, [algorithm] was used to rank [features]
reusable_elements: To reduce the impact of [issue], [Scaler] is used to normalize the data. [Algorithm] was used to rank [features]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not chain Therefore when steps are independent

units.source_excerpt: We use seven XGBoost models to train each associated percentage of (1,2,3,4,5,6,X) for a fixed word, using 'Daily frequency', 'CharNum' and 'Initial letter'.
units.reusable_pattern: We use [N] [models] to train each [category] for [input], using [features]
reusable_elements: We use [N] [models] to train each associated [category] for a fixed [input], using [feature-list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 7 separate models without discussing shared structure

units.source_excerpt: Since our model was based on XGBoost, we need to use sensitivity analysis to measure the uncertainty of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Since our model was based on [technique], we need to use sensitivity analysis to measure uncertainty
reusable_elements: Since our model was based on [technique], we need to use sensitivity analysis to measure [aspect]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim sensitivity analysis required only for specific model types

units.source_excerpt: After much deliberation, we finally settled on an unequally weighted average Ew on every word.
units.reusable_pattern: After much deliberation, we finally settled on [metric] on every [unit]
reusable_elements: After much deliberation, we finally settled on [metric]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'much deliberation' — state criteria for choice

units.source_excerpt: As results shown in Table 3 that the variation range of Ew is within 1%, thus the uncertainty of the model is low.
units.reusable_pattern: As results shown in [Table] that [metric] is within [threshold], thus uncertainty is low
reusable_elements: As results shown in [Table] that the variation range of [metric] is within [threshold], thus the uncertainty is low
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'As results shown' — use 'Table X shows'

units.source_excerpt: Since the distribution of reported results depends mainly on the difficulty of the word, we decided to use the unequally weighted average as the measurement of word difficulty.
units.reusable_pattern: Since [distribution] depends mainly on [factor], we decided to use [metric] as measurement
reusable_elements: Since [distribution] depends mainly on [factor], we decided to use [metric] as the measurement of [concept]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim 'depends mainly on' without multivariate evidence

units.source_excerpt: We found that nearly 60% of the points fell between 600 and 700, while the other 40% was distributed almost evenly on two sides. Thus, we decided classification labels as easy, medium, and hard.
units.reusable_pattern: We found that [X]% of points fell between [A] and [B], while [Y]% on two sides. Thus, labels as [list]
reusable_elements: We found that nearly [X]% of points fell between [A] and [B], while the other [Y]% distributed on two sides. Thus, labels as [list]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not derive classification thresholds from distribution shape alone

units.source_excerpt: We divided the sample data into the training set and the test set with the proportion of 3:1, and trained the RBF kernel SVM model.
units.reusable_pattern: We divided [data] into training and test with proportion [ratio], and trained [model]
reusable_elements: We divided [data] into training and test sets with the proportion of [ratio], and trained [model]
prohibited_generalizations: Specify random seed for reproducibility

units.source_excerpt: After taking it into the model, we got the prediction label of 'EERIE' as 'hard', which was also consistent with the unequally weighted average result in chapter 5.
units.reusable_pattern: After taking [example] into [model], we got label [result], consistent with [prior-result]
reusable_elements: After taking [example] into the model, we got the prediction label as [result], which was also consistent with [prior result] in [section]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim consistency as validation — same data used

units.source_excerpt: They are all above 0.6, reflecting the high accuracy (can be described as higher than 60%) of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: They are all above [threshold], reflecting [quality] of the model
reusable_elements: They are all above [threshold], reflecting the [quality] of the model
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call 60% 'high accuracy' — it is moderate

units.source_excerpt: We chose three words with similar difficulties: 'Royal', 'Sport', and 'Prove', since differences among their daily frequency ranking and average letter frequency are both less than 2%.
units.reusable_pattern: We chose [N] [examples] with similar [qualities]: [list], since differences in [features] are less than [threshold]
reusable_elements: We chose [N] [examples] with similar [qualities]: [list], since differences among their [features] are both less than [threshold]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not test sensitivity with only 3 examples

units.source_excerpt: The model we used (LSTM neural networks) has higher accuracy and better performance than classical methods, such as ARIMA.
units.reusable_pattern: The model we used ([model]) has higher accuracy than classical methods, such as [alternative]
reusable_elements: The model we used ([model]) has higher [quality] than classical methods, such as [alternative]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim superiority without head-to-head comparison in this paper

units.source_excerpt: The impact of special days (such as holidays or the MCM contests) is not taken into account.
units.reusable_pattern: The impact of [factor] (such as [examples]) is not taken into account
reusable_elements: The impact of [factor] (such as [examples]) is not taken into account
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list limitations without discussing potential magnitude

units.source_excerpt: The SVM classification model is weak in recognizing 'hard' words.
units.reusable_pattern: The [model] is weak in recognizing [category] specific weakness acknowledgment
reusable_elements: The [model] is weak in recognizing [category] [items]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state weakness without proposing improvement direction

units.source_excerpt: Dear Puzzle Editor of the New York Times, I'm writing to express our keen interest in the Wordle game on your website.
units.reusable_pattern: Dear [Recipient], I'm writing to express our keen interest in [subject]
reusable_elements: Dear [Recipient], I'm writing to express our keen interest in [subject]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid first-person singular in team letter

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, we used the LSTM model to predict the total number of players in the future. Although the total number will continue to decline, the percentage of hard mode will fluctuate to rise.
units.reusable_pattern: Firstly, we used [model] to predict [target]. Although [trend-A], [trend-B] will [direction]
reusable_elements: Firstly, we used [model] to predict [target]. Although [trend-A], [trend-B] will [direction]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'fluctuate to rise' — unclear direction

units.source_excerpt: Based on these conclusions, we strongly recommend adding a difficulty factor and a reward item to wordle games.
units.reusable_pattern: Based on these conclusions, we strongly recommend adding [feature-A] and [feature-B] to [product]
reusable_elements: Based on these conclusions, we strongly recommend adding [features] to [product]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'strongly recommend' without cost-benefit analysis

units.source_excerpt: Our model and suggestions can help increase awareness and participation in your game. Good luck with your future development.
units.reusable_pattern: Our [models/suggestions] can help increase [outcomes]. Good luck with [future]
reusable_elements: Our [output] can help increase [outcomes]. Good luck with your [future]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'Good luck' in formal academic correspondence

units.source_excerpt: 7-entry reference list: Hochreiter LSTM, Siami-Namini ARIMA-LSTM comparison, Poirrier Wordle decision tree, Selby Wordle strategy, Olah LSTM tutorial, Leipzig Corpora, Notre Dame.
units.reusable_pattern: 7-entry reference list spanning LSTM, Wordle strategy, and NLP corpora
reusable_elements: [N]-entry reference list spanning [topics]
